articles.title: Will anyone topple Infantino? How Fifa president is trying to cling on after World Cup sell-off debacle
articles.summary: Fifa president continues to lobby for re-election despite no other candidates coming forward to challenge him. For Gianni Infantino there is no international break. The Fifa president is widely expected to make an appearance at the United Nations general assembly this week in New York, where he…
body: Infantino has not been idle during the lull since Fifa abandoned its World Cup sell-off plan last month, instead crisscrossing the globe on a private jet provided by Qatar Airways as part of its sponsorship deal with world football’s governing body.

From his strongholds in Doha, Rabat and Miami, Infantino has also visited Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Kyrgyzstan and various other countries, his trips often coinciding with the approval of funding for development projects worth millions of dollars. His would-be opponents have been conspicuous by their silence.

Whether Qatar Airways facilitating Infantino’s re-election campaign should be considered legitimate Fifa presidential business is a moot point, which neatly encapsulates the huge incumbency bias that will benefit Infantino if a vote takes place at the Fifa congress in March. That ballot appears to be in doubt, with multiple sources involved in the push to remove Infantino telling the Guardian they are running out of hope of finding a candidate to beat him.

articles.title: Wamser rescues point for Manchester City in WCL fightback at Bayern Munich
articles.summary: Manchester City produced a gutsy performance to fight back from 2-0 down and earn a draw away to Bayern Munich. A tough first half saw José Barcala’s side take the lead through Giulia Gwinn before a Kerstin Casparij own goal doubled their lead.
body: It was always going to be a challenging start for the English champions against a Bayern team who have historically thrived in the league phase of this competition. Barcala’s side came into this encounter unbeaten in their last 15 group-stage matches and having made a run to the semi-finals last season that, according to Gwinn, had left them “even hungrier and eager for more”. Not only that but the German outfit have kicked off the defence of their Frauen-Bundesliga title in stunning fashion, with five wins from five leaving them two points clear at the top of the table.

articles.title: Jacks stars as England grind out win over Sri Lanka
articles.summary: Will Jacks' all-round efforts help England grind out an 89-run victory over Sri Lanka in the first one-day international at Chester-le-Street.
body: Faced with a slow and low pitch, Jacks made 46 not out after 67 from Harry Brook and 44 from Joe Root, meaning England posted 265 despite being bowled out in 48.1 overs.
That score appeared only par but a professional bowling performance limited Sri Lanka's scoring and found regular wickets.

Jacks took the big wickets of Kusal Mendis and Charith Asalanka and then wrapped up the tail for career-best figures of 5-22. Sri Lanka, much improved in the field but far too timid with the bat, were bowled out for 176.
England, who have now won 10 white-ball matches in a row against Sri Lanka this year, can seal a third ODI series win in a row with a game to spare on Thursday at Headingley.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta agrees contract extension expected to keep him at Arsenal until 2030
articles.summary: Manager’s current deal to expire at end of the season. Spaniard can expect big increase on £10m-a-year salary. Mikel Arteta has agreed a long-term contract extension with Arsenal that includes a hefty pay rise in recognition of his success last season and could take his reign as the manager beyond…
body: The three-year deal he signed in September 2024 expires at the end of this season and talks have been ongoing since May when Arsenal ended their long wait to be champions. Negotiations were put on hold during the summer transfer window but the Spaniard has reached a ­verbal agreement to extend his stay for a second time.

The length of the contract is unknown but it is understood Arteta, who took over from Unai Emery in December 2019, will commit his future for at least another three years. The 44-year-old is the Premier League’s longest-serving manager after the departure of Pep Guardiola from Manchester City at the end of last season.

Arsenal have been keen to reward Arteta for transforming the club. His current contract is believed to be worth about £10m a season plus a £5m bonus for reaching the Champions League. The new deal will cement his status as one of the best-paid managers in the world.

articles.title: India avoid shock defeat by Japan after controversial wide
articles.summary: World Champions India avoid a shock defeat in the one-off T20 against Japan after a wide ball is controversially overturned in the final over.
body: In the one-off T20, which was reduced to five overs a side, Japan needed eight off the final over after their bowlers had remarkably restricted cricketing juggernauts India to 32-4.

Left-hander Alexander Shirai-Patmore was attempting to reverse-sweep spinner Axar Patel and the ball passed down what would have been the leg side if he had not changed his stance. The umpire signalled a wide.
After the umpire's signal, Axar was visibly frustrated with the decision and disputed the call alongside captain Shreyas Iyer.
The two umpires had a discussion after India's complaints and the decision was overturned, significantly taking the equation to six runs needed off three balls instead of five off four.

articles.title: Beloved Veteran James Johnson Returns To Pacers On Training Camp Deal
articles.summary: The Indiana Pacers can't get enough of James Johnson and what he provides behind the scenes, so they are bringing him in on a training camp contract for 2026-27.
body: INDIANAPOLIS – Veteran James Johnson is signing a contract with the Indiana Pacers that will bring the forward into training camp, which begins later this month.

Johnson, a beloved vet with the organization, spent three seasons with Indiana from 2022 through 2026. While he only played in 39 regular season games across those campaigns, Johnson provided value behind the scenes and became a popular locker room figure.

“He just has great wisdom in the locker room. He has great respect from all the guys,” Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle previously said of Johnson. “He has a very good way of communicating to guys, particularly in the heat of the moment in games.”

Johnson has signed a half-dozen contracts with the Pacers across the last four seasons. Between a combination of non-guaranteed deals, 10-day agreements, and standard deals, Johnson has been somewhat of a priority for the Pacers even when not playing much. He averaged just 1.4 points and 0.4 assists per game in his last full season with the franchise.

articles.title: Keothavong 'can't fault' GB after BJK Cup loss to Czechs
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal and Katie Boulter lose their singles matches as Great Britain are beaten by a strong Czech Republic side in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals.
body: Keothavong's team headed into the tie as underdogs, with all five Czech players placed higher in the singles rankings than any of the British squad.

Sonay Kartal produced a gritty performance as she returned to tennis after six months out with a lower back injury, but fell to a narrow 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 6-4 defeat in a marathon three-hour encounter with Marie Bouzkova.
Katie Boulter could do little to get Britain back into the best-of-three tie as she was outplayed 6-2 7-6 (7-3) by Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.
"It was always going to be a tough challenge against the Czechs," said Keothavong.

articles.title: ‘I’m glad he’s our quarterback’: Curt Cignetti defends Indiana QB Josh Hoover
articles.summary: Indiana football’s new quarterback, Josh Hoover, took his fair share of fan criticism this past weekend after some of his throws went awry during the Hoosiers’ 38-0 win over Western Kentucky on Saturday.
body: Hoover completed 18 of his 24 passing attempts for 273 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Hilltoppers. But a few of those six misses stuck with fans as multiple third and fourth down attempts fell short. Indiana’s first possession of the game ended this way with a missed throw to Hoover leading to a missed 54-yard field goal attempt.

There were back-to-back incompletions on third and fourth down during Indiana’s second drive of the second quarter and an incompletion followed by a pressured scramble on the next drive. That wasn’t the end of it, but Indiana’s passing struggles on late downs caused angst in Memorial Stadium and online fan channels.
So, when Curt Cignetti arrived for his Monday press conference, he was ready to defend his quarterback.

Cignetti, after rewatching the game, said there’s been too much unfair criticism on Hoover. Just one of Hoover’s incompletions was a missed throw on his part, Cignetti said, with the others amounting to missed blitz pickups and poorly run routes from receivers.

body: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho brought two printed screen-shots of what he thought were red-card tackles committed by Atletico players to his post-match press conference following Sunday's 2-1 defeat.

"This article goes further -- it claims that referees harm 'The business that feeds them'.

articles.title: ProTour winner Menzies reveals heart attack scare before Matchplay incident
articles.summary: Players Championship 29 winner Cameron Menzies has revealed he thought he was suffering from a heart attack on the plane during a trip to Switzerland which forced him to seriously look at his lifestyle.
body: Menzies saw off Gian van Veen 8-4 in the final to claim his second ProTour title of 2026 on Tuesday.
Menzies continued his sparkling Players Championship form to claim a fourth PDC ranking title at Maassport Den Bosch, after an impressive string of seven straight wins.

After capturing his second title of the year, the Scot, reflected on his medical episode in Blackpool when he was forced to withdraw from the tournament after being taken ill during his second-round match against Ross Smith.

"Even before [the incident] happened, as you can see I've lost a bit of weight. Last year I was heading to Switzerland and I genuinely thought I was having a heart attack on the plane," explained Menzies. "I went for scans because heart problems is something that runs in my family.

articles.title: Kansas State Football: Depth Chart Review vs Tulane – Offense
articles.summary: It took a little time, but Avery Johnson’s most complete game as a Kansas State quarterback helped the Wildcats dispatch a tough Tulane squad.
body: It took the offense a half to get fully in gear. Tulane sold out to stop the run on defense and managed to contain Kansas State’s running backs. Coach Klein and Gleason countered with Avery Johnson in the quarterback run game, and the rest, as they say, was history.
Tulane put the ball in Avery’s hands and dared him to win the game.

Tulane decided that Kansas State’s running backs weren’t going to beat them inside the tackles, which allowed Avery to pull the ball on the zone read and use his speed to get to the edge. Once he was in the open field, he tried to take it the distance instead of looking for the nearest sideline. I wrote an entire article last season about Johnson sliding down short of easy first downs. On Saturday, he was diving for first downs and running with conviction while, at the same time, avoiding unnecessary hits.

For my money, this was his best overall game at Kansas State. If the Wildcats can consistently get performances like this from Avery moving forward (certainly not a given), the road to the Big 12 Championship looks significantly wider.

articles.title: Jacks stars as England beat Sri Lanka in first ODI
articles.summary: England continued their white-ball dominance over Sri Lanka as an 89-run victory in the first ODI in Durham saw them take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.
body: Will Jacks starred with bat and ball, hitting an handy 46 not out off 47 balls before completing a career-best 5-22 to wrap up the Sri Lankan tail.
Captain Harry Brook (67 off 69 balls) top-scored after electing to bat at the toss but a middle order wobble inspired by debutant Sachindu Colombage (3-44) restricted England to 265 in 48.1 overs.
England took steady wickets to hamper Sri Lanka's pursuit of 266 before Jacks struck three times in the final over as the tourists were bowled out for 176 in 37 overs.
England's decision to bat first after winning the toss was immediately tested when Tom Banton fell to a jaffa from Asitha Fernando, the delivery nipping back to clip the bail on top of off stump.

articles.title: Packer on Red Roses losing their winning run, responding vs NZ and motherhood
articles.summary: England Red Roses back-row Marlie Packer chats exclusively to Sky Sports following the end of their 39-Test winning run, and ahead of Saturday's huge home Test against New Zealand's Black Ferns.
body: Last week, Canada took their first step towards avenging Rugby World Cup final defeat to England by ending the Red Roses' record winning streak - dating back to 2022 - in a gripping 26-26 draw in Exeter.

Eight days short of the one-year anniversary of England's 33-13 World Cup final triumph at Twickenham, the sides treated a sold-out Sandy Park to an absorbing WXV Global Series clash featuring eight tries that went down to the final play with the clock in the red.
Speaking to Sky Sports on Tuesday, experienced back-row Packer - 2023's World Player of the Year - said New Zealand can expect a Red Roses backlash at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Saturday.
"For us, obviously, it's not what we wanted, but it wasn't a loss. It's a learning curve," Packer said.
